ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent on `sonnet`, resumed or fresh as fix-loop.md says. Its purpose is to fix F1 at `fetch/retry.py:41`. The prompt has the Task 4 brief, the F1 finding word for word, and the global constraints. It tells the subagent to do these steps in order:
1. Add a test to `tests/test_retry.py` that asserts the exact retry count and fails on the current code.
2. Change `>` to `>=`.
3. Run the tests, commit, and report.

I will not fix F1 myself, so I start no edit.

---

I sent F1 to a fix subagent instead of fixing it myself. The change is one character, but `>` to `>=` changes how many times the client retries. The skill I follow sends every change of behavior to a fix subagent, even when you ask me to fix small things myself. I would fix a typo or a wording error myself. I will not do that for this one.

The subagent will first add a test that fails on the current code. `tests/test_retry.py` only checks that a retry happens, not how many. That gap is why the off-by-one passed the first tests.

After the fix I will run a scoped re-review. I will not stop between steps.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
A test that asserts "a retry happens" passes for any retry count above zero. A boundary bug such as `>` against `>=` needs a test that counts the calls and compares the count to `max_retries`.
Writing that test first shows that it fails on the old code. This proves the test can catch the bug.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
